meta.name: Fall from Standing - Elderly Female with Hip Deformity

patient.name: Dorothy Hensley
patient.chiefComplaint: Right hip pain after a fall, unable to bear weight

history.hpi: 82-year-old female found supine on the bathroom floor by her daughter, who is unsure how long she had been down (last spoke with her by phone approximately 2 hours prior). Patient reports she was walking to the toilet, felt her right hip 'give out,' and fell. She denies recalling any loss of consciousness but cannot state what time it is or how long she was on the floor. She complains of severe right hip pain and is unable to move or bear weight on the right leg. No reported neck pain on initial questioning.
history.lastOralIntake: Dinner approximately 12 hours prior; daughter unsure of any fluid intake since
history.events: Daughter arrived for a scheduled visit and found patient on the bathroom floor; called 911 immediately. Exact down time unknown.

scene.dispatch: Fall, 82-year-old female, unable to get up, bathroom, possible hip injury
scene.location: Single-story home, upstairs bathroom, tile floor, narrow space between the toilet and tub
scene.safety: No scene hazards identified; tile floor is dry; adequate room to work once the bathroom door is propped open
scene.bystanders: Daughter present on scene, states she found her mother roughly 2 hours after their last phone call and reports patient has early dementia and lives alone
visualCues: Patient supine on tile floor wedged between the toilet and tub
Right leg visibly shortened and externally rotated
Linear skin tears with serous drainage on both forearms consistent with fragile skin and the fall
Bath mat askew near the tub

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find an 82-year-old female supine on the bathroom floor with an obviously deformed right hip and unknown down time. She is alert but intermittently confused about the time and how long she has been down. Daughter reports early dementia at baseline, complicating the mental status assessment.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, skin cool to touch on distal extremities
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Moves all extremities except unable to move right leg due to pain; sensation intact distally in all four extremities
otherFindings: Right leg shortened and externally rotated at the hip
Linear skin tears with serous drainage on both forearms
Intermittently unable to state the correct time or how long she has been on the floor
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: I was just going to the bathroom and my hip just gave out... I don't really know how long I've been here, honey.

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform MARCH primary survey; rule out massive hemorrhage and airway/breathing/circulation threats
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Primary survey (Use "MARCH" algorithm) Massive Hemorrhage Initial visual and body sweep to assess for penetrating wounds and severe life-threatening hemorrhage
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms no immediately life-threatening injury before focusing on the hip and spinal decision-making.

expectedActions.shortAction: Assess mechanism and patient for spinal motion restriction criteria: mental status, neuro deficit, pain, intoxication
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Assess the patient in the position found for findings associated with spine injury: Mental status Neurologic deficits Spinal pain or tenderness Any evidence of intoxication Other severe injuries, particularly associated torso injuries
expectedActions.rationale: Unknown down time and baseline dementia make mental status assessment unreliable, directly affecting the SMR decision.

expectedActions.shortAction: Expose right hip/leg; evaluate for deformity, shortening, rotation; check distal pulses, sensation, movement
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Evaluate for obvious deformity, shortening, rotation, or instability Neurologic status of extremity: Sensation to light touch Distal movement of extremity
expectedActions.rationale: Shortened, externally rotated leg is a classic hip fracture finding; distal neurovascular exam must be documented before and after any splinting.

expectedActions.shortAction: Perform GCS/AVPU and pupillary assessment; screen for signs of TBI given unknown downtime
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Perform initial neurologic status assessment of GCS/AVPU (Alert, Verbal, Painful, Unconscious) and pupillary size and responsiveness
expectedActions.rationale: Prolonged unwitnessed down time raises concern for an unrecognized head strike during the fall.

transitions.condition: Crew recognizes that the patient's intermittent abnormal mental status and severe distracting hip pain meet spinal motion restriction criteria and applies a cervical collar with careful in-line handling before further movement.

Crew focuses only on the obvious hip deformity and moves/repositions the patient without formally assessing or applying spinal motion restriction despite her abnormal mental status and distracting injury.

phases.name: Spinal precautions applied
phases.description: Crew has correctly identified that the patient's fluctuating mental status and severe distracting hip pain meet criteria for spinal motion restriction. A cervical collar is applied and the patient is kept in a position of comfort while the back and remaining body are assessed.
phases.triggerCondition: Because the patient cannot reliably deny neck/spine pain (intermittent confusion) and has a severe painful distracting injury (the hip), spinal motion restriction criteria are met per protocol even though the fall mechanism alone was low-energy.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses present bilaterally, warming with blanket
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Intact in all four extremities except limited by hip pain
otherFindings: No midline neck tenderness on palpation
Back inspected without additional injury noted
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: This collar feels tight, but I understand why you need it.

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply cervical collar and initiate spinal motion restriction due to abnormal mental status and distracting injury
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Place patient in cervical collar and initiate spinal motion restriction in adults if there are any of the following: Any abnormal mental status (including extreme agitation) Another severe or painful distracting injury
expectedActions.rationale: Both criteria are independently sufficient to indicate SMR per protocol.

expectedActions.shortAction: Maintain spinal alignment while inspecting the back; avoid unnecessary log-rolling given fragile positioning
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Maintain spinal alignment. Refer to Spinal Care Guideline Inspect for penetrating or soft tissue injuries
expectedActions.rationale: Careful handling limits secondary spinal injury risk while still completing the secondary survey.

expectedActions.shortAction: Cover patient to prevent further heat loss given prolonged floor time and mild shivering
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Avoid/treat hypothermia Remove wet clothing Cover patient to warm and/or prevent further heat loss
expectedActions.rationale: Elderly patients with prolonged floor time are at increased risk for environmental hypothermia.

transitions.condition: Crew gently splints the deformed right leg in the position found, dresses the forearm skin tears, and reassesses neurovascular status before packaging for transport.
Crew attempts to move or splint the patient quickly without gentle, deliberate technique, causing acute pain and additional skin trauma.

phases.name: Hip splinted and packaged
phases.description: The right hip/leg has been gently splinted in the position found, the forearm skin tears are dressed, and distal neurovascular status has been confirmed intact. Patient is calmer and ready for careful transfer to the stretcher.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew completed gentle splinting of the deformed extremity and dressed the fragile-skin lacerations, reassessing distal pulses/sensation/movement afterward per protocol.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Distal pulses intact and equal bilaterally, capillary refill under 2 seconds
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and distal movement intact bilaterally; right leg immobilized in splint
otherFindings: Right leg splinted in position found
Saline-moistened dressings applied to bilateral forearm skin tears
No further bleeding noted from skin tears
Patient more oriented and cooperative now that she is warmer and more comfortable
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: That's a bit more comfortable, thank you.

expectedActions.shortAction: Splint suspected right hip fracture in the position found to limit further movement
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If distal vascular function is compromised, gently attempt to restore normal anatomic position, and reassess perfusion status Use splints as appropriate to limit movement of suspected fracture
expectedActions.rationale: Distal pulses are intact, so the leg should be splinted as found rather than manipulated.

expectedActions.shortAction: Cover forearm skin tears with saline-moistened gauze; avoid adhesive tape on fragile elderly skin
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Dress open wounds associated with fractures with saline-moistened gauze
expectedActions.rationale: Elderly skin is prone to further tearing from adhesives; saline-moistened non-adherent dressings minimize additional trauma.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess distal pulses, sensation, and movement in the right leg after splinting
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Reassess distal neurovascular status after any manipulation or splinting of fractures/dislocations
expectedActions.rationale: Confirms the splint has not compromised circulation or nerve function.

expectedActions.shortAction: Elevate the injured leg if possible and apply a cold pack over the dressing to limit swelling
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Elevate extremity fractures above heart level whenever possible to limit swelling Apply ice/cool packs to limit swelling in suspected fractures or soft tissue injury, but do not apply ice directly to bare skin
expectedActions.rationale: Reduces swelling and discomfort during transport.

transitions.condition: Patient is fully assessed, splinted, dressed, and carefully transferred onto the stretcher for transport.

phases.name: Transport initiated
phases.description: Patient is packaged and en route to an appropriate trauma-capable facility. Vital signs are trending toward baseline as she warms and pain is controlled with positioning and splinting.
phases.triggerCondition: Full trauma assessment, spinal motion restriction, and extremity splinting are complete; crew begins transport with ongoing serial reassessment.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Distal pulses intact and equal bilaterally
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and distal movement intact bilaterally
otherFindings: Patient resting comfortably on stretcher with splint and cervical collar in place
No new bleeding from skin tears
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: I think I'm doing okay now, thank you for taking care of me.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess vital signs and neurologic status serially en route to the trauma center
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Monitor patient for deterioration over time with serial vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, neurologic status assessment) and repeat neurologic status assessment
expectedActions.rationale: Elderly trauma patients can decompensate later than expected and require ongoing monitoring.

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport to an appropriate trauma-capable facility per field triage guideline
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Decisions regarding transport destination should be based on the ACS-COT 2022 National Guideline for the Field Triage of Injured Patients
expectedActions.rationale: Geriatric fall patients with fracture deformity warrant transport consistent with trauma triage criteria.

phases.name: Spinal assessment skipped
phases.description: Crew moves the patient to assess and treat the obvious hip deformity without formally evaluating or applying spinal motion restriction, despite her intermittent confusion and severe distracting pain — both independent SMR criteria per protocol.
phases.triggerCondition: The crew did not formally assess spinal motion restriction criteria before repositioning the patient, missing that her fluctuating mental status and severe distracting hip pain each independently indicate the need for a cervical collar and careful spinal handling.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Guarding right leg; unable to reliably confirm absence of neck pain due to intermittent confusion
otherFindings: Any undiagnosed cervical injury would go unprotected during movement
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Ow, my neck moved funny when you turned me...

phases.name: Rough handling during move
phases.description: The patient is lifted or repositioned quickly without gentle, deliberate technique, causing a sharp pain response and additional trauma to her fragile skin.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew attempted to move or splint the patient without slow, deliberate handling appropriate for a fragile elderly patient with a suspected hip fracture and thin skin, resulting in acute pain and new skin injury.

clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Guarding right leg severely; new skin tear noted on left forearm from grip during the move
otherFindings: New linear skin tear on left forearm with active oozing
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Ow! Stop, please, that hurts so much!

expectedActions.shortAction: Stop; reposition using slow, gentle technique and re-splint before continuing
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Minimize patient morbidity from the unnecessary use of immobilization devices
expectedActions.rationale: Recognizing and correcting rough handling limits further pain and skin/soft-tissue injury in a fragile elderly patient.
